turns.doctor_question: Hello, welcome in. What brings you into the clinic to see me today?
turns.patient_response:
Hi, doctor. Thank you so much for taking the time to see me today, I really appreciate it. 

Um, well, I hope I'm explaining this right, but... I've been noticing—or rather, my family and colleagues have pointed out—that I have a little bit of a habit of not staying in my chair. Like, during staff meetings at the high school where I teach, or even just sitting around the dinner table. I'll suddenly get up when everyone else is perfectly fine just staying seated. 

I always try to make it look like I'm just being helpful, you know? Like I'll pop up to refill the coffee pot, or I'll walk to the back of the room to double-check a handout. But... well, if I'm being completely honest, nothing is ever really urgent. I just sort of suddenly feel like I need to be up and moving. 

It feels a little silly to admit that at my age, honestly. I hope I'm not making too big a deal out of it... is that the sort of thing you were looking to know?

symptom_reasoning.S011: The patient explicitly states they have a habit of not staying in their chair and getting up during meetings or dinners when expected to remain seated.
symptom_reasoning.S012: The patient describes a sudden internal feeling that they 'need to be up and moving', which indicates restlessness.

turns.doctor_question: Besides needing to be up and moving, do you also find it difficult to keep your focus or attention on tasks?
turns.patient_response:
Oh, um, no, actually. I hope that doesn't make things more confusing, but my focus is really quite good. 

I mean, I spend hours grading essays and writing up lesson plans, and I always try to make sure I'm being very thorough. I don't really lose track of my work or anything like that. I really pride myself on being on top of things for my students. 

It's really just... well, my body just wants to be moving while I'm doing things, if that makes sense? I can pay perfect attention to what the principal is saying at the meeting, I just... happen to be standing by the coffee maker while I listen. 

Does that make sense? I hope it's okay that I don't have the focus issue you mentioned... I just want to make sure I'm giving you the right information.

symptom_reasoning.S011: The patient mentions standing by the coffee maker during meetings instead of remaining seated.
symptom_reasoning.S012: The patient states that their body just wants to be moving while they are doing things, indicating physical restlessness.
symptom_reasoning.S001: The patient denies making careless errors, stating they are very thorough with their work.
symptom_reasoning.S002: The patient explicitly denies difficulty sustaining attention, noting they can spend hours focused on grading and lesson plans.
symptom_reasoning.S003: The patient denies not listening when spoken to, stating they can pay perfect attention to the principal during meetings.

turns.doctor_question: When you feel that urge to get up and move, do you notice any uncomfortable or unpleasant sensations in your legs specifically?
turns.patient_response:
Oh, um... no, not really. I hope I'm understanding you correctly, but no, it's not like a pain or an ache or anything uncomfortable like that. 

It's more just... a feeling of energy, I guess? Like my legs just have a little too much pep in them and they want to stretch. It doesn't hurt or bother me, it's just... a preference to be moving. 

I'm sorry, I hope that's a helpful answer. I don't want to mislead you into thinking I'm having leg cramps or anything like that. Is that what you were asking about?

symptom_reasoning.S012: The patient describes a feeling of energy and a preference to be moving, which indicates a subjective feeling of restlessness.

turns.doctor_question: Do you often find yourself worrying excessively about a number of different everyday things, to the point that it feels hard to control?
turns.patient_response:
Oh, goodness, no. I hope that's okay, but I really don't consider myself a worrier at all. 

I mean, naturally, teaching high school means there are always little things to keep track of, but... no, I never feel like I'm worrying excessively or that anything is out of my control. I try very hard to just stay positive and handle whatever comes my way with a good attitude. 

I really hope I'm giving you the right information... I just wouldn't want to give you the impression that I'm an anxious person when I'm really quite content, aside from just needing to move around a bit. Is that what you were asking?

symptom_reasoning.S056: The patient explicitly states they do not consider themselves a worrier and never feel like they are worrying excessively.
symptom_reasoning.S057: The patient explicitly denies feeling that anything is out of their control regarding worry.

turns.doctor_question: Did you have this same habit of being constantly on the move or having trouble staying seated back when you were a child, before the age of 12?
turns.patient_response:
Oh, um... yes, actually, I suppose I did. I hope it doesn't sound like I was a naughty child or anything! I really always tried my best to be good. 

My report cards always made a point to say I was a very bright girl, which my parents were quite proud of... but, well, the teachers did sometimes have to write that I couldn't quite stay in my seat, or that I had trouble waiting my turn. It was never out of disrespect, I promise! I think it was just... enthusiasm, really. 

My mother actually used to joke that I wore a little path right into the floorboards between my desk and the pencil sharpener before I was even ten years old. I just liked to keep my pencils sharp and stay busy, I suppose! 

Does that... is that the kind of childhood information you were looking for? I just want to make sure I'm giving you exactly what you need.

symptom_reasoning.S011: The patient explicitly states that teachers noted she couldn't stay in her seat.
symptom_reasoning.S014: The patient confirms being constantly on the move as a child, noting she wore a path between her desk and the pencil sharpener.
symptom_reasoning.S017: The patient mentions that her report cards indicated she had trouble waiting her turn.
